## Summarize

**Research question:** How does obesity prevalence vary across income and racial/ethnic groups among adults in NHANES?

```{r}
# AI prompt: Help me adapt the starter code to compare obesity prevalence across income and racial/ethnic groups among adults.
# Verified: I checked the column names and ran the code to review the counts and obesity percentages.
obesity_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
  Age >= 18,
  !is.na(BMI),
  !is.na(IncomeGroup),
  !is.na(Race)
) |>
mutate(
  Obese = BMI >= 30
) |>
group_by(IncomeGroup, Race) |>
summarise(
  n = n(),
  obese_count = sum(Obese),
  obesity_prevalence = mean(Obese) * 100,
  .groups = "drop"
)

obesity_summary
```
The summary shows that obesity prevalence varies across both income and racial/ethnic groups. In this sample, non-Hispanic Black adults had some of the higher obesity percentages across the income groups. These results are descriptive, so I would not use them to say that income or race causes obesity.

## Function

```{r}
# AI prompt: Help me understand and reuse a function that summarizes a numeric variable.
# Verified: I ran the function on both BMI and Age and checked that it returned a count and mean for each.
mean_with_n <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    n = sum(!is.na(x)),
    mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

mean_with_n(nhanes$BMI)
mean_with_n(nhanes$Age)
```
The function worked on both BMI and Age, showing that the same calculation can be reused for different numeric variables.
